chunks: As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Bint Ilyas, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
'Do not pray less than forty-four.' He said: And I saw him praying four rak'at after al-'atamah.

There is no prohibition in this report against what exceeds forty-four; rather, he (peace be upon him) prohibited only that it be reduced below it. And there is nothing preventing him from encouraging these forty-four due to their being emphasized, while encouraging what is beyond them through another hadith. We have previously presented hadiths that encompass that.

key_terms.أَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ: forty-four — the minimum prescribed number of rak'at, referring to the recommended daily prayers (nafilah) beyond the obligatory
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: al-'atamah — the Isha (late night/evening) prayer, one of the five daily prayers; an archaic Arabic term for the night darkness
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: rak'at — individual units of the ritual prayer cycle (salat)
key_terms.نَهْيٌ: prohibition — a jurisprudential term for legal interdiction; here a nahi tahrimy establishing a minimum floor

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the minimum number of rak'at to pray, and how does Sheikh al-Tusi interpret this ruling in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This entry from al-Istibsar presents 'Abdullah ibn Sinan's first-hand report that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibited praying fewer than forty-four rak'at, and that the Imam himself was observed performing four rak'at after the 'atamah (Isha). Sheikh al-Tusi then offers a jurisprudential reconciliation: the prohibition establishes a minimum, not a ceiling, and separate hadiths already cited in the work encourage additional voluntary prayers beyond forty-four.
word_analysis: due to their being emphasized / confirmed
through / by means of a hadith
